about: Chronoa task eval: what a person says, and the tool call a correct assistant makes. Checked, never executed. Each 'expect' entry is one acceptable call: 'tool' must match, and every key in 'args' must match its rule - a number equals (5 == 5.0), a string is compared case-insensitively and may be a list of acceptable values, a string starting with '~' must be contained, '*' only requires the key to be present. 'none': true means no tool should be called. 'ask': true also accepts ask_user. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL: fewer skills have at least one case than the tree registers, so a regression in tool selection is visible in most of the list and invisible in the rest. The exact counts live in `coverage` beside this text and are asserted by `test_the_recorded_coverage_is_still_the_coverage`, which is why the prose here does not repeat a number that a new skill would make stale. It was complete when it was last claimed; `tools/gen_eval_cases.py --check` reports what is missing, and this stops saying PARTIAL when that output is empty. `tools/gen_eval_cases.py --check` reports what is missing and `tests/test_task_eval.py` asserts the counts against this file. THIS FILE: a broad generated set (2026-10-15) - 915 everyday requests covering all 259 skills, written by a model from the tool list and checked by script (every tool and argument exists; repeated requests removed). Run it with `task_eval.py --file tools/eval_cases_1000.json`; tools/eval_cases.json stays the hand-checked set.
